biography: Rodrigo Antonio Pupo's journey began amidst the vibrant chaos of Sao Paulo's streets. His father, a mechanic with a deep love for classic Volkswagens, instilled a passion for speed and precision from a young age. Rodrigo spent his childhood dismantling and reassembling engines in his father's garage, gaining an intuitive understanding of mechanics that would later prove invaluable on the track. He started racing in local karting events at 16, quickly earning a reputation for his fearless overtaking maneuvers and relentless pursuit of victory. The transition to the Copa Fusca series was a natural progression, where his aggressive style both thrilled crowds and frustrated rivals. A defining moment came during the 2018 Interlagos race when, despite starting last due to a mechanical issue, he clawed his way through the field to secure a podium finish. Currently, Rodrigo is a prominent figure in the Copa Fusca scene, consistently challenging for race wins and championships, and constantly pushing the limits of his machine and his own abilities. He aspires to move to higher classes of racing, but his love for the Copa Fusca keeps him coming back.
drivingStyle: Pupo is known for his aggressively late braking and willingness to take risks. He thrives in close-quarters combat, often executing daring overtakes in corners where others wouldn't dare. His tire management is decent, but his focus tends to be on maximizing pace in the early stages of a race, sometimes to the detriment of his tires later on. He is remarkably composed under pressure, rarely cracking even when facing intense competition or mechanical setbacks. Pupo is a fighter through and through, always pushing for every last tenth of a second.

famousQuote: "Racing isn't just about speed; it's about heart. If you don't have the heart to fight, you don't belong on the track."
careerHighlight: Winning the 2019 Copa Fusca Championship after a season-long battle with Ricardo Silva, securing the title with a daring last-lap overtake at Curitiba.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead in the 2020 Interlagos race due to a mechanical failure, losing valuable championship points and suffering a minor injury.
